reports.title: David White
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The safety briefing during nursing handover is now to include a verbal handover of the care plans for patients assessed as at risk of falls to alert incoming staff members as to the risk and care plan.
promises.summary: Add verbal handover of care plans for fall risk patients during nursing handover.

promises.quote: daily auditing of all nursing and falls risk documentation must be carried out.
promises.summary: Daily auditing of nursing and falls risk documentation.

promises.quote: Multidisciplinary Team meetings on Ward 9F have now been changed to earlier in the day to discuss patients and make effective action plans for patient at risk of falls.
promises.summary: Change MDT meetings to earlier for fall risk patients.

promises.quote: A practice development team has been recruited to support ward staff in adhering to ward protocols and procedures including documentation, assessment of risks and communication.
promises.summary: Recruit practice development team to support ward staff.

promises.quote: facilitated training from the 'Falls Lead' for the Trust to re-train nurses regarding the fall procedure and management and this took place on 29 June 2015.
promises.summary: Facilitated Falls Lead training for nurses on fall procedures.

promises.quote: Site managers can now be contacted out of hours to ensure appropriate management of care.
promises.summary: Allow out-of-hours contact with site managers for fall risk patient management.

concerns.quote: The effect of Heparin, in causing confusion, was not in the records, and therefore not acted upon.
Nursing notes documented a risk of falls/mobilisation and action to be taken, but there was no supervision arrangement in place. One to one care had been in contemplation.
concerns.hazard: lack of supervision for fall risk

concerns.quote: Whilst nursing notes were being kept about the risks, the records were not being reviewed and acted upon.
concerns.hazard: failure to review and act on nursing notes

reports.title: Iris Fordham: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The poor quality of recording clinical records impeded the Trust's governance processes, in that the author of a serious incident investigation was unable to rely on clear evidence to understand why essential actions were not carried out in Ms [name redacted] care.
The Trust failed to complete a falls risk assessment of Ms Fordham.
The consequence of (2) was that no falls care plan was completed.

The fact that the failures at (2) & (3) were not detected and remediated by successive clinical staff members suggests that they did not read essential parts of the clinical record when providing care. The cumulative failings, on the part of multiple healthcare professionals suggests a culture of indifference inimical to the provision of safe and effective practice.
The Trust has not considered any step to resolve individual failings in care through disciplinary or regulatory channels.
concerns.hazard: lack of disciplinary or regulatory action
